The Islam West Africa Collection

A digital archive of the press, periodicals, recordings and documents in which Islam and Muslims in West Africa are written about and debated, built at the Leibniz-Zentrum Moderner Orient (ZMO) in Berlin. The chapters below say what it holds, where and when it comes from, and what it speaks of.

What it holds

Newspaper articles sit beside Islamic periodicals, audiovisual recordings, archival documents, photographs and a bibliography of scholarly references. An index of people, organisations, places, subjects and events links them together.

Where it comes from

Each item is filed under the country of the newspaper, institution or channel it comes from. The bibliography of scholarly references is not counted by country.

The years it covers

Each dated item is counted in its year of publication. The bars show what the collection holds, not how much was published at the time.

Languages and subjects

Most items are in French, the language of most of the region’s press. The index tags each item with the people, organisations, places, subjects and events it concerns; the lists give those tagged most often.

The scholarship it gathers

Beside its sources, the collection is a bibliography of the scholarship on Islam and Muslims in West Africa: books, journal articles, chapters, theses and reports, each catalogued with its authors, date and type. The bars count them by decade of publication: what the bibliography holds, not all that has been written.
